articles.title: Member Recognition
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) recognized several volunteers at its February 15th annual meeting for their significant contributions. Individuals such as Phil Chambers, Terry Kahl, Carl Reisinger, Bill and Susan O'Neil, Frank Geefay, Richard Stone, and Paul Mancuso were honored for their diverse efforts, ranging from technical support and program development to extensive public outreach and website migration. Their dedication highlights the crucial role volunteers play in the success of SJAA's various programs and community engagement.

articles.title: SJAA MEMBER IMAGE: SUPERNOVA IN M82!
articles.summary: Paul Colby and Marion Barker successfully imaged the supernova in M82, a galaxy 11 million light-years away, capturing data on January 25, 2014. They detailed their astrophotography setup, which included a Celestron C8 and Canon T3i, and their evolving technique of controlling the camera via laptop and stacking images using FIGI. The supernova remained bright at visual magnitude 11, making it visible with moderate amateur telescopes.

articles.title: NASA's $8 billion Hubble Successor is Set for 2018 Launch
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), an $8 billion successor to Hubble, is set for a 2018 launch after overcoming delays and budget issues. This large infrared telescope, with its 6.5-meter primary mirror, is an international collaboration poised to study the universe from its earliest moments to the formation of life-supporting solar systems. It incorporates several innovative technologies, including a folding segmented mirror and ultra-lightweight beryllium optics.

articles.title: News Briefs
articles.summary: Scientists have successfully produced the first complete global geologic map of Ganymede, Jupiter's largest moon, more than 400 years after its discovery. Separately, an Expedition 38 crew member aboard the International Space Station captured a nighttime photograph of the Sochi Olympic Park, clearly showing Fisht Olympic Stadium and the Olympic flame.

articles.title: KID SPOT
articles.summary: This "Kid Spot" section provides astronomy-themed entertainment and educational content for children. It features space jokes, a short quiz on astronomical facts, and a "Night Sky Challenge" for March 2014, detailing the visibility of several planets.

articles.title: Constellations
articles.summary: This article provides an overview of the constellation Gemini, one of the 88 modern constellations and part of the zodiac. It details its historical recognition by Ptolemy, its position relative to other constellations, and notable astronomical features like the Eskimo and Medusa Nebulae, as well as the Geminid meteor shower. The piece also delves into the Greek and Babylonian mythological associations of Gemini, particularly the twins Castor and Pollux.

articles.title: Solar Observing
articles.summary: This article highlights the importance of safe solar observing and recounts a successful "Sol Saturday" event held at Campbell Park on January 25, 2014. Members of SJAA shared views of sunspots and active regions through various filtered telescopes with around 75 kids and adults, noting excellent public engagement despite minor parking challenges. The piece also mentions regular monthly solar programs.

articles.title: Club Updates
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is launching several new initiatives including a library program, an advanced learner telescope program for members to evaluate equipment, and a 'Fix-It' program for equipment repairs. The club also announced upcoming events such as the annual Club Auction, Earth Day Festival, and Astronomy Day, alongside a schedule of dark sky observing events. Board meeting excerpts highlight discussions on light pollution at Houge Park, exploring alternative viewing sites, and re-election of board members, with open board seats still available.
